newsitem.title: UK: No horse play as animals blessed at London church.
newsitem.headline: No horse play as animals blessed at London church.

text.p: Cats, dogs, goldfish, snails and horses were blessed by a vicar at a London church on Thursday while their owners and a choir sang "Bare Necessities" -- the theme tune from the Disney film, "The Jungle Book."
People and pets from all over Britain's capital city gathered at the candlelit parish church of St Stephen with St John for the annual service to hear the Reverend Ralph Godshall.
"We've gathered here with our animals to get ready for Christmas," he told the congregation.

"We've got the manger out. Since the setting for Christ's birth is a stable, we're bringing animals which are part of our community to affirm that our lives are made up of animals as well as human beings."
Under the 19th century Anglican church's limestone canopy, Godshall sprinkled holy water on a wide variety of pets, including a goldfish called Flounder.

The fish's owner, Nelly Kidd, 8, was glad of the blessing but wasn't sure if Flounder noticed the extra water in its jam-jar aquarium. "I'm not sure. I don't even know if Flounder is a boy or a girl," Kidd said.
Ann Mercer, 73, owner of a 13-year old spaniel called Tuppence, was in no doubt that the ceremony was important for both man and beast.
"Tuppence suffers from a bad heart and her kidneys are packing up (malfunctioning)," Mercer said. "Last year she came and was blessed and lived. I have faith in it."
A police horse, based in Scotland Yard's stables just a brief canter away from Prime Minister John Major's Downing Street residence, was among the four-legged flock given the annual blessing.
The 15-year-old chestnut Ogilvey, who normally works crowd control during riots and football matches, remained calm throughout the hour-long service.
"He's very happy. Nothing is being thrown at him tonight," Ogilvey's police handler, Tony McMaster, said.
